messages.author: cd8f249492ca9d15
messages.subject: instability with cloglog link
parts:
Hi, I'm fitting a cloglog linked model, but finding lots of errors and fitted values all near 1. Fitting with a logit link works fine. A reproducible example is below. The usual tricks of using EB, large diagonal, and refitting haven't worked in my real-world example, though adding a stronger prior on the random effects and then re-fitting without that prior produces reasonable results...though I'm having a hard time replicating that in an example to share. 

It makes me suspect that an optimizer is getting stuck somewhere, though it is pure speculation on my part... I don't know how the cloglog link is represented internally, and whether cancellation of log's and exp's is used in the log likelihood for binomial models, but that as a source of numerical instability struck me as a possible issue looking at inla.link.invcloglog(x).

##
library(INLA)
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(2)
#10 samples from each of 100 sites
n <- 100
m <- 10
df <- expand_grid(site_id = 1:n, sample_id = 1:m) %>%
    mutate(
        site_effect = rnorm(n, 0, 1)[site_id],
        sample_effect = rnorm(nrow(.), -4, 1.5),
        eta = 2 + site_effect + sample_effect,
        mu = binomial('cloglog')$linkinv(eta),
        N = 1,
        y = rbinom(nrow(.), N, mu)
    )
#fails, restarts, and ends up with wild estimates for site_id precision:
mod_cloglog <- inla(y ~ f(site_id) + offset(sample_effect),
    N = N,
    family = "binomial",
    control.family = list(link = "cloglog"),
    data = df
)
mod_cloglog$summary.hyperpar

#fitted values are all nearly 1:
mod_cloglog$summary.fitted.values$mean %>% summary()

#logit seems to work fine:
mod_logit <- inla(y ~ f(site_id) + offset(sample_effect),
    N = N,
    family = "binomial",
    control.family = list(link = "logit"),
    data = df
)
mod_logit$summary.hyperpar

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] instability with cloglog link
parts:
thank you, Arie

the rescue operation did not succeed well (as you noted), based on this
example I modify it to try and intermedidate stage first, like the
common trick for non log concave likelihoods,

r = inla(..., control.inla=list(cmin=0))
r$.args$control.inla$cmin = -Inf
r = inla.rerun(r)

you can check the change here

https://github.com/hrue/r-inla/commit/da640b94c312cbab2234c16d35519e32dfae988c

this seems to work well.

it will be available in the next build, next week I guess, when I'm back
at KAUST

Best
H
